Match the set before the card name

A Magic card name can appear in several sets and treatments. The same artwork can also appear on a reprint. Start with the small printed details instead of selecting the first result with the right name.

  1. Read the card name. If the image is hard to read, use the name as a search term rather than guessing the letters.
  2. Find the set symbol or printed set code and copy the full collector number. Keep leading zeros, letters and other printed parts.
  3. Compare the candidate image with the frame and artwork on your copy. Check the border and treatment as well as the illustration.
  4. Match the language and physical finish. A photograph that hides the foil reflection cannot settle that field.
  5. Open the exact record. Read the source, currency, price date and condition or existing slab-grade context.

Resolve an old printing without a visible collector number

If your card has no printed collector number, search by name and inspect the set symbol, artwork, border and copyright line. Use those features together to narrow the release. Do not invent a number to make the card fit a result.

A copyright year helps with comparison, but it does not replace the release identity. If two candidate records still look similar, keep both open and compare their images with the physical card. A result for a later reprint is not a value for an earlier copy.

Check foil, borderless and showcase treatments separately

Foil, non-foil, borderless, extended-art and showcase descriptions can identify different printings. Some differences concern the frame or artwork; others concern the reflective surface. Confirm the treatment visible on the card and the finish available on its catalog record.

Tilt the physical card under even light to inspect reflection. Keep glare out of the identification photo. A bright lamp reflection across a normal card is not evidence of a foil treatment, and a dark photograph can hide a real foil finish.

If the candidate has the right name and set but a different frame, return to the results. Do not use that candidate's price until you resolve the printing. The record, language and finish must describe the copy you own.

Fix a wrong MTG scan match

  • Right name, wrong set: enter the printed set code and collector number in MTG text lookup. Compare the set symbol on the card with the result.
  • Right image, wrong treatment: compare the full border, frame and foil surface. Search the treatment shown on the card rather than choosing the highest price.
  • No useful result: retake a straight-on photo of one card front. Remove nearby cards from the image and keep the edges visible.
  • No published price: retain the identified record. A missing amount is not zero, and another edition's amount is not a substitute.

Organize copies after identification

Keep different sets and treatments as separate holdings in the iPhone app. Confirm quantity, raw condition or the grade already on a slab. Two copies of the same printing can still need different holding details when their condition or grading state differs.

The app can queue up to 10 separate card photos for review. Photograph each card separately, then confirm or remove the results before starting another group. This app queue is different from the single-photo web tool and does not provide extra free scans.

A portfolio reference total uses the confirmed holdings and available published prices. It does not establish what a buyer will pay for the entire collection. For a sale or trade, compare the exact printing and condition with the price context you are using.

Look up a card without scanning it

Use the MTG catalog when you already have the name or number. Open the matching record to inspect available price references and dates. The card price checker explains how raw condition, an existing grade and the source affect the comparison.

MTG card scanner questions.

Can the MTG card scanner tell reprints apart?

The scan suggests records with the set and collector number, not just the card name. Review those details and confirm the treatment before using that printing's price.

Does CardScanFox handle foils and alternate treatments?

Match the catalog record and finish for the copy you own. Keep foil, non-foil, borderless and showcase printings separate when those records are available. A scan does not confirm a physical foil surface by itself.

Can I track MTG and Pokemon cards in the same collection?

Yes. The iPhone app can organize confirmed holdings from Magic, Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece and other supported categories. Its reference total uses the available published prices for those holdings.

Can I use it as an MTG card price checker without scanning?

Yes. Search the MTG catalog by name, set or collector number, then open the exact printing for its available price and date. Personal holdings and collection totals are managed separately in the app.
